title: Hypertrophy Q&A #4
summary: NH answers viewer hypertrophy questions: calisthenics vs weighted compounds, ab and arm supersetting, grease the groove, clavicle frame genetics, irrelevant vs evolving rep ranges, neck training, novice and Bulgarian programs, barbells vs dumbbells, tonnage sacrifice, CNS fatigue myths, incline curls, symmetry and imbalances. Central theme: train the whole body with intensity, volume and frequency, and judge recovery by your own body.
claims: Pure calisthenics leaves gains on the table because it lacks a hip hinge and heavy weighted knee flexion, shortchanging glutes, hamstrings, lower back and rhomboids
A size program needs a vertical press, horizontal press, knee flexion, hip hinge, horizontal pull and vertical pull, since these cover the bulk of the musculature
Abs can be added to any training day because the core is involved in every movement; train them as often as you can
A dedicated ab day is a monumental waste of time; never go to the gym just for abs
Small muscle groups like abs do not need long rest; superset them or put them in giant sets instead of resting three minutes
On heavy deadlift or back days the core is already taxed, so do less direct ab work; leg raises are still fine to stretch the abs and decompress the spine
He does not preach 'volume equals mass'; he preaches intensity, volume and frequency together, because volume without weight selection becomes junk volume
Grease the groove (popularized by Pavel) works for pull-ups because they are low impact and the upper back recovers fast; it is an exception, not the rule
Grease the groove on bench, squat or deadlift produces shoulder, knee and lower back pain because those lifts need recovery between sessions to rest the structures
Applied to weighted movements, grease the groove turns into nucleus overload, which is impractical for compounds because they stimulate too many muscles at once
Grease the groove is mostly low-intensity junk volume: great for learning a movement fast, but once technical mastery peaks it stops being effective
Wrist and joint size matter little for bodybuilding: smaller joints make the surrounding muscle look bigger
Small wrists do not limit arm size; with under 6.5 in wrists he has 13.5+ in forearms and arms that look massive
Clavicle length is the key frame indicator because it is an absolute measurement that dictates shoulder width; you can build delts to look wider but a narrow frame stays narrow
Clavicle angle is genetic: upward-pointing clavicles leave less room for traps, downward ones leave more room but create sloped shoulders
Parallel clavicles are better for trap display, while upward-pointing clavicles tend to give the separated, capped shoulder look
Exercise cannot change clavicle angle, but training upper chest, traps and shoulders changes how the clavicular area looks
The deadlift is one of the best, if not the best, exercises for growing the entire body, contrary to claims it is bad for hypertrophy
Never do a single set of biceps or triceps then rest; superset them with each other or with another movement to save time and accumulate more volume
Find pairings that balance endurance, performance, progression and injury prevention, e.g. a press followed by a long-head triceps exercise, or a press followed by face pulls
A waist indent above the hips can be reduced by losing fat and building obliques and the sides of the abs, which creates continuity and a V-taper
To fix an hourglass look, work rib cage expansion with lots of pullovers to build the lats, and train the core to sculpt it rather than fearing it will look worse
Nucleus overload is high frequency, high volume, low intensity; its name is marketing, and grease the groove is a widely different method
A relevant rep range is one whose intensity drives strength progression and therefore hypertrophy; high rep ranges are typically irrelevant
In a 20-rep set the first 10-12 reps must be easy, so roughly half the set is spent at irrelevant intensity; the late difficulty is relative intensity from fatigue, not absolute intensity
High-rep sets are often limited by cardiovascular endurance or technical breakdown rather than the muscle, so fibers are not really challenged
Evolving rep ranges require choosing weight jumps, exercises, sets and reps, then beta-testing the scheme on paper first; novices should not use them
Neck bridges certainly build the neck, but for bodybuilders he recommends neck curls in every direction instead because a neck injury is the one you most want to avoid
Tendons are always under some stress in training; the idea of directing all stress only to the muscle is a pipe dream
Bulgarian 'lite' is really a Wisconsin-style method: practicing one lift daily builds strength on it but unbalances the body, since no single movement trains everything
The deadlift trains the upper back less effectively than most think and ignores whole portions of it
A novice doing jiu-jitsu five times a week should not do Bulgarian-style training; two to three compound-focused sessions a week plus grip, core, neck and bridging work suits him better
A 19-year-old three months into lifting should not be getting injured; injured novices testify to how bad popular novice programs are
His own novice program is deliberately lower impact so beginners have room to adapt it to their own goals
Ignoring load, barbells have the edge over dumbbells because their technical interaction with the body (bar path, grip) opens more pathways, though it requires upfront investment
Front and lateral raises and strict curls are better with dumbbells, because the arms can stay at the sides; barbell curls push the weight forward and recruit the front delts
Most so-called novice programs are actually powerlifting programs with an agenda; Body by Rings similarly grooms you into a rings specialist
A teen whose calling is bodybuilding should pick an open program mixing weights and calisthenics; heavy specialization makes later transitions a hassle

Tonnage can dip temporarily (tonnage sacrifice) with evolving rep ranges, but per the tonnage stability principle the dips must be minor; bodybuilders maintain and add small increments rather than peaking
Tonnage should increase weekly rather than through scheduled monthly peaks, which tend to cause plateaus by forcing strength artificially
You do not need a rest day for your CNS; if your muscles feel ready, keep training and let your body be the judge
He has deadlifted and squatted heavy for a year and a half with nonstop strength progress and no CNS burnout
Supposed CNS burnout is usually injury or mismanaged volume and intensity: people expect strength their training never actually built
Like overtraining, CNS burnout is not something most people are even capable of reaching
Skipping legs does not make the upper body grow more; the lower body provides leg drive and stability that let the upper body express its strength
Specialists like arm wrestlers grow huge forearms and biceps because extra time on one part builds endurance and more training, not because other parts are untrained
A muscle spoiled by lots of attention will shrink if that attention is withdrawn
Incline dumbbell curls force light weight and most people bounce out of the bottom using tendon elasticity; they should never be the main biceps progression lift
Do curls and most movements standing to engage the core; EZ-bar and barbell curls are better for biceps strength progression
Symmetry is a personal choice; he wants shoulders smaller than arms, pecs not overpowering and legs bigger than the rest
Humans are biologically drawn to symmetry, and a balanced body also prevents injury
Fix a lagging side with a low-impact unilateral exercise: extra lighter reps after intense sets, or 3-4 extra sets at session end, with more volume rather than more weight
A big stomach at low body fat is usually bloating: poorly digested foods, water retention, two huge meals stretching the stomach, or poor breathing; building the core makes it look smaller
He admires pro bodybuilding as the pinnacle of the sport but would not want those bodies; his favorite real physiques are Serge Nubret and Sergio Oliva's arms, plus Guts and Zodd from Berserk
You can emphasize heads of a muscle via joint angles, but compounds resist being turned into isolations; do compounds safely, heavy and frequently, then hammer lagging parts with isolation volume
